name: Affine set
description: A set that contains the entire line through any two of its points, i.e. is closed under affine combinations (coefficients summing to one).

name: Affine hull
type_signature: subset of R^n → affine subset of R^n
description: The set of all affine combinations of points of a given set, equivalently the smallest affine set containing it.

name: Convex set
description: A set that contains the line segment between any two of its points, i.e. is closed under convex combinations.

name: Convex hull
type_signature: subset of R^n → convex subset of R^n
description: The set of all convex combinations of points of a given set, equivalently the smallest convex set containing it.

name: Convex cone
description: A set closed under all conic (nonnegative) combinations of its points, equivalently closed under nonnegative scaling and addition.

name: Conic hull
type_signature: subset of R^n → convex cone in R^n
description: The set of all conic combinations (nonnegative-coefficient combinations) of points of a given set, the smallest convex cone containing it.

name: Hyperplane
type_signature: {x in R^n : a^T x = b}, a ≠ 0
description: The codimension-one affine set of points satisfying a single nontrivial linear equation a^T x = b.

name: Halfspace
type_signature: {x in R^n : a^T x ≤ b}, a ≠ 0
description: The convex set of points satisfying a single nontrivial linear inequality a^T x ≤ b, one of the two regions a hyperplane divides space into.

name: Euclidean ball
description: The convex set of points within Euclidean distance r of a center x_c.

name: Ellipsoid (set)
description: The convex set obtained by an invertible linear image of a Euclidean ball, parameterized by a center x_c and positive-definite shape matrix P.

name: Second-order (norm) cone
description: The convex cone of vector–scalar pairs whose vector part has Euclidean norm bounded by the scalar part, also called the ice-cream or Lorentz cone.

name: Polyhedron
description: The solution set of finitely many linear inequalities and equalities, equivalently an intersection of finitely many halfspaces and hyperplanes.

name: Simplex
description: The convex hull of k+1 affinely independent points, the simplest bounded polyhedron of a given affine dimension.

name: Positive semidefinite cone
description: The convex cone of symmetric n×n positive semidefinite matrices within the space of symmetric matrices.

name: Intersection preserves convexity
description: The intersection of any collection of convex sets is convex.

name: Affine image and preimage preserve convexity
description: The image and the inverse image of a convex set under an affine map are convex.

name: Perspective function
description: The map P(x,t)=x/t on the domain t>0 whose image and inverse image preserve convexity of sets.

name: Linear-fractional function
function_signature: (x with c^T x + d > 0) → ((Ax+b)/(c^T x + d))
description: The composition of an affine map with a perspective function, f(x)=(Ax+b)/(c^T x+d), which preserves convexity of sets on its domain.

name: Separating hyperplane theorem
description: Any two disjoint convex sets can be separated by a hyperplane with one set in each closed halfspace.

name: Dual cone
type_signature: K^* = {y : y^T x ≥ 0 for all x in K}
description: The set of vectors making a nonnegative inner product with every element of a cone K, itself always a closed convex cone.

name: Self-dual cones
description: The nonnegative orthant, the second-order cone, and the positive semidefinite cone each equal their own dual cone.

name: Proper cone
description: A convex cone that is closed, solid (nonempty interior), and pointed (contains no line).

name: Generalized inequality
description: The partial order x ⪯_K y defined by y − x ∈ K for a proper cone K, generalizing componentwise and matrix inequalities.

name: Minimum and minimal elements
description: For a generalized inequality, a minimum element is comparable to and below all others, while a minimal element has no other element strictly below it.

name: Dual characterization of minimal elements
description: A point is minimal for ⪯_K if it minimizes λ^T x over the set for some strictly dual-feasible λ ≻_{K^*} 0 (with a converse for minimum elements).

name: Convex function
description: A function whose domain is convex and which satisfies f(θx+(1−θ)y) ≤ θf(x)+(1−θ)f(y) for all θ in [0,1].

name: Concave function
description: A function whose negative is convex, equivalently satisfying the reversed convexity inequality.

name: Extended-value extension
function_signature: (convex f on dom f) → (f : R^n → R ∪ {+∞})
description: Extending a convex function to all of R^n by assigning value +∞ outside its domain, simplifying handling of domains in convexity statements.

name: First-order condition for convexity
description: A differentiable function on a convex domain is convex iff f(y) ≥ f(x) + ∇f(x)^T(y−x) for all x, y in the domain.

name: Second-order condition for convexity
description: A twice-differentiable function on a convex domain is convex iff its Hessian is positive semidefinite (∇²f ⪰ 0) throughout the domain.

name: Epigraph
type_signature: {(x,t) : x in dom f, f(x) ≤ t}
description: The set of points lying on or above the graph of a function, which is convex iff the function is convex.

name: Nonnegative weighted sum and integral preserve convexity
description: A nonnegative weighted sum, or weighted integral, of convex functions is convex.

name: Composition with an affine map preserves convexity
description: If f is convex then g(x)=f(Ax+b) is convex.

name: Pointwise maximum and supremum preserve convexity
description: The pointwise maximum of finitely many, or supremum of an arbitrary family of, convex functions is convex.

name: Scalar composition rules
description: Conditions on the monotonicity and convexity of h and g under which the composition f(x)=h(g(x)) of scalar functions is convex.

name: Vector composition rules
description: Conditions on h and the component functions g_i under which the composition f(x)=h(g_1(x),...,g_k(x)) is convex.

name: Partial minimization preserves convexity
description: If f(x,y) is jointly convex and C is convex, then g(x)=inf_{y in C} f(x,y) is convex in x.

name: Perspective of a function
description: Forming g(x,t)=t f(x/t) from a function f, which is convex whenever f is convex.

name: Quasiconvex function
description: A function on a convex domain all of whose sublevel sets are convex, equivalently f(θx+(1−θ)y) ≤ max{f(x),f(y)}.

name: First-order condition for quasiconvexity
description: A differentiable f on a convex domain is quasiconvex iff f(y) ≤ f(x) implies ∇f(x)^T(y−x) ≤ 0.

name: Log-concave and log-convex functions
description: A positive function is log-concave (log-convex) if its logarithm is a concave (convex) function.

name: K-convex function
description: A vector-valued function convex with respect to a generalized inequality ⪯_K, satisfying f(θx+(1−θ)y) ⪯_K θf(x)+(1−θ)f(y).

name: Standard-form optimization problem
description: The canonical statement of minimizing an objective f_0 subject to inequality constraints f_i ≤ 0 and equality constraints h_j = 0.

name: Convex optimization problem (standard form)
type_signature: min f_0(x) s.t. f_i(x) ≤ 0, a_j^T x = b_j
description: A standard-form problem with convex objective and convex inequality constraint functions and affine equality constraints.

name: Optimality condition for convex problems
description: For a convex problem with differentiable objective, a feasible x is optimal iff ∇f_0(x)^T(y−x) ≥ 0 for every feasible y.

name: Equivalence transformations
description: Reformulations such as variable change, constraint substitution, slack variables, or epigraph form that preserve a problem's solution set.

name: Quasiconvex optimization via bisection
function_signature: (quasiconvex problem, tolerance) → (optimal value via convex feasibility subproblems)
description: Solving a quasiconvex problem by bisecting on the objective value and checking convex feasibility of each sublevel set.

name: Linear-fractional program
type_signature: min (c^T x + d)/(e^T x + f) s.t. linear constraints
description: A quasiconvex program minimizing a ratio of affine functions over a polyhedron, reducible to a linear program.

name: Quadratic program (QP)
type_signature: min (1/2)x^T P x + q^T x s.t. Gx ⪯ h, Ax = b, P ⪰ 0
description: A convex problem minimizing a convex quadratic objective subject to affine inequality and equality constraints.

name: Quadratically constrained quadratic program (QCQP)
type_signature: min convex quadratic s.t. convex quadratic ≤ 0, Ax = b
description: A convex problem with a convex quadratic objective and convex quadratic inequality constraints.

name: Second-order cone program (SOCP)
type_signature: min f^T x s.t. ||A_i x + b_i||_2 ≤ c_i^T x + d_i, Fx = g
description: A convex problem minimizing a linear objective subject to second-order cone constraints.

name: Robust linear program
type_signature: min c^T x s.t. a_i^T x ≤ b_i for all a_i in uncertainty set
description: A linear program with constraints required to hold for all parameter values in an uncertainty set, reducing (e.g. for ellipsoidal uncertainty) to an SOCP.

name: Geometric program (GP)
description: An optimization problem in posynomial and monomial functions that becomes convex under a logarithmic change of variables and objective.

name: Semidefinite program (SDP)
type_signature: min c^T x s.t. x_1 F_1 + ... + x_n F_n + G ⪯ 0, Ax = b
description: A convex problem minimizing a linear objective subject to a linear matrix inequality (matrix-valued affine constraint in the PSD cone).

name: Conic (cone) program
type_signature: min c^T x s.t. Fx + g ⪯_K 0, Ax = b
description: A convex problem in conic form with a linear objective and a generalized inequality constraint with respect to a proper cone K, generalizing LP, SOCP, and SDP.

name: Vector (multicriterion) optimization
description: An optimization problem whose objective is vector-valued and minimized with respect to a generalized inequality induced by a proper cone.

name: Pareto optimal point
type_signature: feasible x with f_0(x) minimal wrt ⪯_K
description: A feasible point of a vector optimization problem whose achieved objective value is minimal, i.e. no feasible point does at least as well in every component and strictly better in some.

name: Scalarization
function_signature: (vector optimization problem, weight λ ≻_{K^*} 0) → (scalar problem min λ^T f_0)
description: Finding Pareto optimal points by minimizing the scalar objective λ^T f_0(x) for dual-feasible weight vectors λ ≻_{K^*} 0.

name: Lagrangian
type_signature: L(x,λ,ν) = f_0(x) + Σ λ_i f_i(x) + Σ ν_j h_j(x)
description: The weighted sum of the objective and constraint functions of an optimization problem, with Lagrange multipliers λ and ν on the constraints.

name: Lagrange dual function
description: The infimum of the Lagrangian over x, a concave function of the multipliers that lower-bounds the optimal value for λ ⪰ 0.

name: Lagrange dual problem
description: The convex problem of maximizing the Lagrange dual function over nonnegative inequality multipliers, yielding the best lower bound on the primal optimal value.

name: Weak duality
description: The optimal value of the dual problem is always a lower bound on the optimal value of the primal problem, for any problem.

name: Duality gap
description: The nonnegative difference between the primal and dual optimal values; zero exactly when strong duality holds.

name: Strong duality
description: The condition that the dual optimal value equals the primal optimal value (zero duality gap), which holds for convex problems under a constraint qualification.

name: Slater's condition
description: A constraint qualification stating that strict feasibility of a convex problem (a point strictly satisfying the nonlinear inequalities) implies strong duality.

name: Geometric/epigraph interpretation of duality
function_signature: (primal problem) → (supporting-hyperplane view of the value function)
description: Interpreting the dual function and duality gap via supporting hyperplanes of the set of achievable constraint–objective value pairs.

name: Complementary slackness
description: At a primal–dual optimal pair with zero duality gap, each inequality multiplier and its constraint cannot both be nonzero (active).

name: Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions
description: The system of primal feasibility, dual feasibility, complementary slackness, and stationarity of the Lagrangian that is necessary, and for convex problems sufficient, for optimality.

name: Max-min (saddle-point) interpretation of duality
description: Expressing primal and dual optimal values as inf-sup and sup-inf of the Lagrangian, with strong duality corresponding to a saddle point.

name: Strong max-min equality (Sion's minimax theorem)
description: For a function convex in one argument and concave in the other over suitable convex sets, the order of inf and sup can be exchanged.

name: Theorems of alternatives via duality
function_signature: (system of inequalities) → (dual feasibility certificate of infeasibility)
description: Deriving theorems of alternatives by applying Lagrange duality to a feasibility problem so that exactly one of a primal system and a dual system is solvable.

name: Sensitivity (shadow price) interpretation
description: Under strong duality and differentiability, optimal dual variables equal the negative partial derivatives of the optimal value with respect to constraint right-hand sides.

name: Perturbation and global sensitivity analysis
function_signature: (constraint perturbations (u,v)) → (bounds on perturbed optimal value p*(u,v))
description: Using optimal dual variables to bound how the optimal value changes under tightening or loosening of the constraints.

name: Duality for generalized inequalities
description: The extension of Lagrange duality to problems with generalized-inequality constraints, using dual-cone multipliers λ ⪰_{K^*} 0.

name: SDP and cone program duality
description: The explicit primal–dual pair and strong-duality conditions for semidefinite and conic programs, with matrix or cone-valued dual variables.

name: Norm approximation problem
description: The problem of minimizing the norm of the residual Ax − b, whose form (LP, QP, etc.) depends on the chosen norm.

name: Chebyshev (minimax) approximation
description: Norm approximation in the ℓ∞ norm, minimizing the largest residual magnitude, expressible as a linear program.

name: Penalty function approximation
type_signature: min Σ φ(r_i), r = Ax − b
description: Minimizing a sum of a convex penalty function applied to each residual (e.g. quadratic, ℓ1, deadzone, or Huber penalty).

name: Regularized (Tikhonov) approximation
description: A bi-objective approximation that trades off residual norm against a regularization term penalizing the solution size; the squared-ℓ2 case is Tikhonov regularization.

name: Robust least squares
type_signature: min sup_{A in uncertainty set} ||Ax − b||_2
description: Least-squares approximation minimizing the worst-case residual over uncertainty in the data matrix A, reducible to an SOCP or SDP.

name: Maximum likelihood estimation as a convex problem
description: Formulating maximum likelihood estimation as maximizing a concave log-likelihood, hence a convex optimization problem, for log-concave models.

name: MAP estimation as a convex problem
description: Maximum a posteriori estimation cast as maximizing a concave log-posterior (log-likelihood plus log-prior) when the posterior is log-concave.

name: Optimal experiment design
type_signature: min (over measurement fractions) scalar of error covariance
description: Choosing measurement proportions to minimize a scalar measure (D-, A-, or E-optimality) of the estimation error covariance, formulated as an SDP or logdet program.

name: Chebyshev center
type_signature: center of the largest ball inscribed in a polyhedron
description: The center of the largest Euclidean ball contained in a convex set, computable by linear programming for a polyhedron.

name: Maximum volume inscribed ellipsoid
type_signature: max log det B s.t. ellipsoid {Bu + d : ||u|| ≤ 1} ⊆ C
description: The largest-volume ellipsoid contained in a convex set, found by a convex logdet maximization program.

name: Minimum volume enclosing (Löwner-John) ellipsoid
type_signature: min log det A^{-1} s.t. set ⊆ {x : ||Ax + b|| ≤ 1}
description: The smallest-volume ellipsoid containing a given set, the Löwner-John ellipsoid, found by a convex logdet program or SDP.

name: Linear discrimination
type_signature: find (a,b) : a^T x_i − b > 0, a^T y_j − b < 0
description: Finding a separating hyperplane that strictly classifies two point sets, a linear-programming feasibility problem.

name: Support vector machine
type_signature: min (1/2)||a||^2 + C Σ u_i s.t. margin/slack constraints
description: Robust linear discrimination maximizing the classification margin (with slack penalties for nonseparable data), a convex quadratic program.

name: Projection onto a convex set
type_signature: min ||x − x_0|| s.t. x in C
description: Finding the point of a convex set nearest to a given point, a convex problem (QP or SOCP depending on the norm and set).

name: Floor planning (placement)
type_signature: convex/geometric program over cell positions and sizes
description: Arranging non-overlapping rectangular cells to minimize bounding-box area subject to placement constraints, formulated as a convex (geometric-programming) problem under a fixed relative ordering.

name: Strong convexity
description: The assumption that a function's Hessian is bounded below by a positive multiple of the identity, giving a quadratic lower bound used in convergence analysis.

name: Line search (exact and backtracking)
function_signature: (point x, descent direction Δx) → (step size t > 0)
description: Choosing the step length along a descent direction, either by exact minimization or by backtracking (Armijo) until sufficient decrease is achieved.

name: Gradient descent method
description: A descent method that at each step moves along the negative gradient direction Δx = −∇f(x) with a line search.

name: Steepest descent method
description: A descent method using the normalized direction of steepest decrease with respect to a chosen norm, of which gradient descent is the Euclidean-norm case.

name: Newton step and Newton decrement
description: The Newton search direction obtained from the Hessian and gradient, together with the Newton decrement that measures proximity to optimality and serves as a stopping criterion.

name: Newton's method (damped and pure)
description: An affine-invariant descent method using the Newton step with a damped (line-search) phase followed by quadratically convergent pure Newton steps near the optimum.

name: Self-concordant function
description: A convex function whose third derivative is bounded by its second derivative to the 3/2 power (and its multidimensional restriction along lines), the Nesterov-Nemirovski property enabling complexity bounds independent of constants.

name: Convergence analysis for self-concordant functions
description: A bound on the number of Newton iterations to minimize a self-concordant function that depends only on the initial gap and the Newton tolerance, free of unknown problem constants.

name: Newton system via factorization and structure
description: Computing the Newton step by Cholesky or other factorization of the Hessian, exploiting sparsity or block structure for efficiency.

name: KKT system (Newton system for equality constraints)
description: The block matrix linear system whose solution gives the Newton step for an equality-constrained minimization.

name: Newton's method with equality constraints
description: Newton's method for minimizing a function subject to affine equality constraints, generating feasible iterates by solving the KKT system at each step.

name: Infeasible-start Newton method
description: A Newton method that uses the combined primal–dual residual and need not start at a feasible point, attaining feasibility and optimality together.

name: Newton step via elimination
description: Solving the equality-constrained Newton/KKT system by eliminating variables to reduce it to a smaller positive-definite system.

name: Logarithmic barrier function
description: A smooth convex function that grows to infinity as x approaches the boundary of the inequality-feasible set, used to approximate indicator constraints.

name: Central path
description: The curve of minimizers, parameterized by t > 0, of the objective plus a scaled logarithmic barrier, converging to an optimal point as t → ∞.

name: Central path suboptimality bound
description: A central path point is no more than m/t suboptimal, where m is the number of inequality constraints, via an associated dual feasible point.

name: Barrier method (SUMT)
function_signature: (convex problem, strictly feasible start) → (approximately optimal point)
description: An interior-point method that solves a sequence of barrier-augmented problems along the central path with geometrically increasing t, also known as the sequential unconstrained minimization technique.

name: Barrier method convergence and complexity
description: A bound on the number of centering steps, and hence Newton iterations, the barrier method needs to reach a given accuracy, polynomial for self-concordant barriers.

name: Phase I (finding a strictly feasible point)
function_signature: (constraints) → (strictly feasible point or certificate of infeasibility)
description: An auxiliary optimization that minimizes the maximum constraint violation to compute a strictly feasible starting point for an interior-point method.

name: Primal-dual interior-point method
description: An interior-point method that updates primal and dual variables simultaneously by solving the perturbed KKT (modified Newton) equations, without an explicit inner centering loop.

name: Surrogate duality gap
description: A computable gap used in primal–dual methods that equals the actual duality gap when the iterates are primal and dual feasible.

name: Generalized-inequality interior-point methods
description: Extensions of barrier and primal–dual interior-point methods to cone programs using generalized logarithmic (e.g. −log det) barriers for the second-order and PSD cones.

name: Schur complement
function_signature: (block matrix [[A,B],[B^T,C]] with A ≻ 0) → (S = C − B^T A^{-1} B)
description: The matrix S = C − B^T A^{-1} B obtained by eliminating a block from a partitioned matrix, used in factorization and elimination.

name: Schur complement characterization of positive semidefiniteness
description: For A ≻ 0, the block matrix is positive semidefinite iff its Schur complement is, converting nonlinear matrix inequalities into linear matrix inequalities.

name: Convexity of the matrix-fractional function
description: The matrix-fractional function x^T Y^{-1} x is jointly convex in x and the positive-definite matrix Y.

name: Concavity of log-determinant
description: The function log det X is concave on the cone of symmetric positive-definite matrices.
